🎙 ‘Childhood is a right, not a casualty of war’: Iranian Embassy in London

📌 London, IRNA – The Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in London has paid tribute to children killed in military attacks in Minab and Lamerd and highlighted the suffering of children in Gaza, stressing that childhood is a fundamental right that must not become a casualty of war.

In a post on its X account marking World Children’s Day on Thursday, the embassy paid tribute to the girls of Minab, “whose lives were cut short by American missiles,” and the children of Lamerd, “whose game of volleyball became their last.”
​
It also remembered 14-month-old Zahra Golpayegani, who died alongside her grandfather, Iran’s Martyred Leader Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei.
​
Referring to the situation in Gaza, the embassy said, “Gaza’s children, who survived the bombs, only to face cold, rain and flooded tents.”
​
The post also recalled children poisoned by Saddam Hussein’s chemical weapons, which were supplied by Germany.
​
The embassy also paid tribute to “every child whose dreams were buried beneath the rubble of war,” noting “Childhood is a right, not a casualty of war.”
​
World Children’s Day is observed annually on November 20, marking the adoption of the Declaration of the Rights of the Child in 1959 and the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989 by the United Nations General Assembly.
